我最早談及 iPhone 影片防震功能令我印象深刻，是 2021 年測試 iPhone 13 Pro 時的事。自此之後，這項功能大幅改良，iPhone 17 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro 都配備了蘋果稱為「超穩定影片」的版本。

雖然聽起來不像某些功能那樣吸引眼球，但它對手持拍攝時 iPhone 的實用性帶來翻天覆地的改變——而我最近的測試正好清楚展示它今天有多出色……

I always carry a small tripod and GorillaPod with me, and use them whenever I know I'll be shooting iPhone video, but of course one of the iPhone's biggest advantages is that it's the camera you always have on you. Sometimes I spot a filming opportunity but haven't brought a tripod.

Often you can improvise – leaning the iPhone against a railing, bracing your body against a lamp post or something similar. But sometimes I've had to rely purely on the iPhone's built-in video stabilisation, and on a recent shoot with the iPhone 18 Pro I was genuinely blown away.

A boat trip along the Thames made for a perfect demonstration of how the iPhone's built-in video stabilisation can actually outperform a tripod. The reason is that boats pitch and roll quite noticeably, and with a tripod the boat itself would stay steady while the scenery around it bobs about. The iPhone, by contrast, locks solidly onto the outside world, letting the boat rock in the foreground.

This ability to hold the horizon rock-steady regardless of how the platform is moving is something even a normal gimbal can't manage. Most consumer-grade models can only smooth motion rather than eliminate it. True horizon-locking requires high-end professional gimbals, plus the gyro-stabilised mounts designed for marine and helicopter use.

The iPhone 18 Pro's Ultra Stable Video mode quite honestly delivers that level of performance as a standard feature built into the stock camera app, with no external hardware required. It's honestly hard to believe.
